messages:
Eli (integration): Hey team — onboarding AcmeApp. We're seeing a flood of 429s right after our client starts (Electron app). Using web SDK v1.4.0, ephemeral keys rotate every 60s. Example: `HTTP/2 429` and header `x-rate-limit-reset: 30`. Happens during the first minute when many clients connect. Any quick ideas?

Maria (CS): Thanks Eli — can you paste the minimal init snippet you're using and confirm how many parallel renderer processes you spawn? Also, are you doing a preflight check per window/tab?

Eli (integration): Minimal snippet: `const r = new Redwood({ key: EPHEMERAL_KEY }); await r.init();` We spawn 4 renderer processes per user for offline sync. Preflight enabled by default via the SDK.

Sam (SDK): pinging @Eli — 4 parallel inits + 60s short-lived tokens is a classic preflight stampede. Two quick mitigations: 1) splay/serialize init so only 1-2 inits happen concurrently per machine. 2) increase ephemeral TTL (ideally to 5m) while onboarding.

Sam (SDK): if you can change config, try:
```js
const client = new Redwood({
  key: process.env.EPHEM_KEY,
  initConcurrency: 2, // cap concurrent SDK init attempts
  preflight: { enabled: true, maxConcurrent: 1, jitter: true }
});
await client.init();
```

Jordan (SRE): To add: our rate limiter tracks short windows for preflight and handshake. When many parallel connections hit auth + preflight at once you see the `x-rate-limit-reset` header with small reset values. Backoff + jitter is the right pattern. If you need immediate relief, we can temporarily raise the onboard window for your account — want to do that while you roll out the init splay?

Maria (CS): Action items: 1) Eli — try Sam's `initConcurrency` + jitter change in staging. 2) If security allows, increase ephemeral TTL to 5m for onboarding. 3) Eli send a short call window and we'll enable a temporary rate-window bump. I'll also collect logs: set `RW_LOG_LEVEL=onboard-debug` and share the trace.

Eli (integration): I can do `initConcurrency` today and request TTL change from security. Quick question: is there a recommended server-side keepalive so renderer processes reuse the same handshake?

Sam (SDK): Yes — enable `keepAlive: true` on the client and persist a singleton per electron main process, then proxy requests to renderers. Example: `new Redwood({keepAlive:true})`. That reduces handshake fanout drastically.

Eli (integration): Great — will try both and report back in ~30m. Thanks.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Deployed SDK v1.4.1 to staging (contains initConcurrency option and improved jitter defaults)

Maria (CS): Nice — @Eli once you try staging, paste a snip of the `onboard-debug` logs (only meta, strip PII) and we'll check the reset headers and decide on a temporary window bump.

Eli (integration): Will do. Appreciate the quick triage! :thumbsup:
